## Summary for recruiters and hiring managers

- Leads platform engineering end to end: cloud foundations, Kubernetes, CI/CD, observability, security and compliance, cost, and on-call.
- Has managed a team of five platform engineers and owned SLAs, mentoring, and performance growth.
- Consistently turns platform work into measurable outcomes: 90% shorter deploy lead time, $216K/year in engineering hours saved, $113K/year in cloud savings, p95 latency cut 50%.
- AI-native way of working: runs coding agents in parallel with strict guardrails, which roughly doubled his merged PRs per month.
- Strong fit for: companies scaling AI products on Kubernetes, teams preparing for SOC 2 or enterprise customers, organizations moving to GCP or modernizing CI/CD, and teams that want to adopt AI coding agents safely.

## Experience

### Cooklist — Head of Platform Engineering (Dec 2025 – present, Austin, TX)
Cooklist builds agentic commerce for grocery: AI search and chat used by enterprise grocery retailers, plus a consumer pantry and meal app.
- Owns the GKE platform across production, staging, and disaster recovery for agentic search, AI chat (streamed over GraphQL WebSockets), and the core Django/Celery API.
- Per-PR ephemeral environments: a Helm release per pull request with pre-seeded Postgres images promoted by digest.
- Trunk-based release pipeline with migration gates, statement timeouts, release-version checks, and a guarded hotfix lane.
- LLM-reviewed database migrations: deterministic lock and table-size analysis plus an LLM verdict on deploy timing, posted on every PR.
- Queue-aware autoscaling: KEDA on Redis streams and Pub/Sub, HPA on custom Prometheus metrics, split health probes, graceful shutdown, PDBs.
- Moved agentic search from gunicorn/Django to FastAPI/Uvicorn with concurrency gates and a load-tested capacity envelope.
- Zero-downtime edge cutover to a Traefik Gateway behind Cloud Armor using weighted DNS; Cloud Armor policies and alerts in Terraform.
- Chef, a hosted Slack agent with intake, engineering, review, and knowledge roles, plus a knowledge skill that keeps engineering docs current from Slack threads and merged PRs.
- Self-hosted GitHub Actions runners (ARC) on GKE spot nodes; Trivy scanning, Renovate, protected branches, Workload Identity Federation for keyless CI.
- Security and compliance: SOC 2 readiness, enterprise security questionnaires, Auth0 and Microsoft Entra SSO with group-synced permissions, AlloyDB IAM auth, Security Command Center.
- Observability and cost: Datadog APM and cost trimming, Google Managed Prometheus with Sev1/2/3 routing to Slack, Sentry volume reduction (~800K fewer events per cycle), a self-hosted status page with DR, committed-use discount reviews.
- Internal engineering docs platform on Cloud Run behind IAP with preview deploys, shipped in about two days.

### Pager — Lead Platform Engineer (May 2022 – Nov 2025, Chicago, IL)
- Led a team of five platform engineers; owned SLAs, project delivery, mentoring, and performance guidance.
- Migrated 60 services to a modern continuous deployment platform: 90% shorter lead time, ~1,800 hours and $216K saved per year.
- Led the move from Spinnaker to Harness with canary and blue/green releases.
- Led on-prem to GCP migration, including containerizing .NET applications off physical racks.
- PostgreSQL to CloudSQL: $80K+ compute savings, p95 −50%, p75 −73%.
- MongoDB to Atlas (7% lower cost), plus upgrading 19 NodeJS services for a major Atlas version.
- $113K/year in cloud savings (disk cleanup, storage right-sizing); $9,600/year from streamlined database version management.
- HIPAA and SOC 2 compliance; production alerting on 14 criteria; multi-cloud Kubernetes on GCP and AWS with Terraform.

## How he works with AI

- Runs Claude Code and Codex in parallel git worktrees: one ticket, one worktree, one agent, with sub-agents for research, tests, and review.
- Roughly doubled merged PRs per month after moving to parallel agents (about 8/month in Feb–Apr 2026 to about 17/month in Jun–Sep 2026); about 63% of his merged PRs in 2026 are AI co-authored.
- Authored 15 reusable agent skills shared across tools: read-only SRE incident triage, postmortem drafting, read-only production database access, AI chat validation, CI fixing, PR review handling, and session handoff (park/pickup).
- Built Chef (`cooklist-chef[bot]`), a hosted Hermes agent fleet that works alongside the team in Slack. It has four roles: a company role for Slack intake, incident triage from alert channels, and Kanban routing; an engineering role that implements changes and opens pull requests; an Elder role that reviews pull requests; and a knowledge role for research and docs. Work is tracked on a Kanban board (optionally linked to Linear), tools are allowlisted and read-only by default, and nothing merges without human approval.
- Paired Chef with a knowledge-curation skill: every week it reviews drive-by Slack conversations, merged GitHub pull requests, and Linear context, validates each candidate against code and config, and opens docs PRs that update the page owning the topic, with decision markers explaining what was decided and why. Routine status noise and speculation are filtered out.
- Guardrails he insists on: diagnose read-only first, staging before production, separate "CI passed" / "deployed" / "live-validated", and nothing merges without human approval.

## Architecture interests

Multi-account AWS and EKS designs (shared networking, Transit Gateway, PrivateLink, VPC Lattice), database-as-a-service platforms, disaster recovery (including Kafka replication and offset consistency), Redis and Postgres scaling, and infrastructure standardization.

## Working style

Practical and implementation-oriented. Thinks in failure modes, migration plans, cost, operational burden, and security before "how do I make it work." Prefers exact commands, Terraform, and YAML over generic advice, makes a clear recommendation, and revises it when new evidence arrives. Hands-on, skeptical of vague answers, and willing to dig until a decision is defensible.
